edges.description: The type 2 response drives blood eosinophilia.
Airway type 2 inflammation is epidemiologically associated with childhood asthma.
The eosinophilic response forms granulomatous inflammation around larvae.
Visceral larva migrans presents with fever.
Hepatic larval migration and granulomas enlarge the liver in VLM.
Hepatic/visceral larval migration causes abdominal pain in VLM.
Pulmonary larval migration causes cough in VLM.
Pulmonary larval migration causes wheezing in VLM.
Ocular granuloma causes tractional retinal detachment.
The ocular granuloma causes visual loss in ocular toxocariasis.
Ocular toxocariasis commonly presents with strabismus.
The retinal granuloma can present as leukocoria.
CNS invasion produces myelitis, the commonest neurotoxocariasis form.
Neurotoxocariasis is epidemiologically associated with epilepsy.

nodes.description: In humans, a non-definitive paratenic host, the larvae cannot complete their life cycle; they undergo prolonged somatic migration through liver, lung, eye and brain and persist in the tissues, continuously releasing excretory-secretory (TES) antigens that provoke the host response. This is the step that produces the systemic and organ-specific disease.

nodes.description: Eosinophil-rich, granulomatous inflammation forms around the migrating or dead larvae, injuring tissue and producing the organ-specific disease: visceral larva migrans (fever, hepatic lesions), ocular toxocariasis (a retinochoroidal granuloma with tractional retinal detachment), and neurotoxocariasis (eosinophilic meningoencephalitis, with an epidemiological link to epilepsy).
